questions.prompt: Which GIAC certification is most directly the foundational, Windows-focused forensics certification that Level 2 of this academy maps onto?
questions.explanation: GCFE (Certified Forensic Examiner) is the foundational Windows-forensics certification — evidence acquisition, user activity, browser artifacts — the standard first step before GCFA.

questions.prompt: GCFA is tied to which SANS course, and builds on which certification as a starting foundation?
questions.explanation: GCFA maps to SANS FOR508 (Advanced Incident Response, Threat Hunting, and Digital Forensics) and is the advanced step up from GCFE.

questions.prompt: Why does GNFA extend beyond what this academy's own Network Forensics level (Level 7) covers?
options: GNFA doesn't actually relate to network forensics at all
Level 7 deliberately stops at log- and flow-level evidence, not full packet capture — which is where GNFA's fuller discipline picks up
GNFA is a beginner certification that Level 7 already exceeds
GNFA only covers cloud networking, unrelated to this academy's Windows scope
questions.explanation: Level 7 is intentionally scoped to logs and flow records, not full packet dissection — GNFA (tied to SANS FOR572) is where that deeper packet-level discipline actually lives.

questions.prompt: Is completing every lesson in this academy a prerequisite for starting certification study?
options: Yes, GIAC requires proof of academy completion
No — by the time Levels 2 and 5 specifically are complete, the GCFE/GCFA study foundation already exists
Yes, but only for GCIH specifically
No, certification study should always come before any hands-on practice
questions.explanation: The lesson is explicit that this isn't a requirement — Levels 2 and 5 alone already build the core GCFE/GCFA foundation.
